1→#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
     2→#
     3→# check-figure-sizes.R — Analyze a .qmd file for figure readability issues
     4→#
     5→# Parses code chunks to extract fig-width, fig-height, theme base_size,
     6→# and facet structure. Calculates effective rendered text size assuming
     7→# the browser displays the figure at a given page width (default 10 inches).
     8→#
     9→# Usage:
    10→#   Rscript check-figure-sizes.R <file.qmd> [display_width_inches] [min_pt]
    11→#
    12→# Arguments:
    13→#   file.qmd              Path to the .qmd file to check
    14→#   display_width_inches  Assumed browser display width in inches (default: 10)
    15→#   min_pt                Minimum acceptable effective text size in pt (default: 6)
    16→
    17→library(argparser)
    18→
    19→p <- arg_parser("Check figure text sizes in a Quarto .qmd file")
    20→p <- add_argument(p, "qmd_file", help = "Path to .qmd file")
    21→p <- add_argument(p, "--display-width", default = 10,
    22→                  help = "Assumed browser display width in inches")
    23→p <- add_argument(p, "--min-pt", default = 6,
    24→                  help = "Minimum acceptable effective text size in pt")
    25→args <- parse_args(p)
    26→
    27→lines <- readLines(args$qmd_file)
    28→
    29→# --- Extract code chunks with their options ---
    30→# Find chunk starts: ```{r}
    31→chunk_starts <- grep("^```\\{r", lines)
    32→chunk_ends   <- integer(length(chunk_starts))
    33→
    34→for (i in seq_along(chunk_starts)) {
    35→  # Find the closing ``` after this chunk start
    36→  candidates <- grep("^```\\s*$", lines)
    37→  candidates <- candidates[candidates > chunk_starts[i]]
    38→  if (length(candidates) > 0) {
    39→    chunk_ends[i] <- candidates[1]
    40→  } else {
    41→    chunk_ends[i] <- length(lines)
    42→  }
    43→}
    44→
    45→# --- Parse each chunk ---
    46→results <- list()
    47→
    48→for (i in seq_along(chunk_starts)) {
    49→  start <- chunk_starts[i]
    50→  end   <- chunk_ends[i]
    51→  chunk_lines <- lines[start:end]
    52→  chunk_code  <- paste(chunk_lines, collapse = "\n")
    53→
    54→  # Extract label
    55→  label_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    56→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*label:\\s*([^\\n]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
    57→  label <- if (length(label_match) > 0) {
    58→    sub("#\\|\\s*label:\\s*", "", label_match)
    59→  } else {
    60→    paste0("chunk-line-", start)
    61→  }
    62→
    63→  # Extract fig-width and fig-height from #| options
    64→  fw_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    65→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*fig-width:\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
    66→  fh_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    67→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*fig-height:\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
    68→
    69→  fig_width  <- if (length(fw_match) > 0) {
    70→    as.numeric(sub("#\\|\\s*fig-width:\\s*", "", fw_match))
    71→  } else {
    72→    7  # knitr default
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  fig_height <- if (length(fh_match) > 0) {
    76→    as.numeric(sub("#\\|\\s*fig-height:\\s*", "", fh_match))
    77→  } else {
    78→    5  # knitr default
    79→  }
    80→
    81→  # Extract base_size from theme_*() calls
    82→  base_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    83→    regexpr("theme_\\w+\\(\\s*base_size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code,
    84→            perl = TRUE))
    85→  base_size <- if (length(base_match) > 0) {
    86→    as.numeric(sub(".*base_size\\s*=\\s*", "", base_match))
    87→  } else {
    88→    NA  # Will use document-level default
    89→  }
    90→
    91→  # Check for absolute text sizes (element_text with size = <number>)
    92→  abs_size_matches <- gregexpr(
    93→    "element_text\\([^)]*size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE)
    94→  abs_sizes <- regmatches(chunk_code, abs_size_matches)[[1]]
    95→  has_absolute_sizes <- length(abs_sizes) > 0
    96→  absolute_size_values <- if (has_absolute_sizes) {
    97→    as.numeric(sub(".*size\\s*=\\s*", "", abs_sizes))
    98→  } else {
    99→    numeric(0)
   100→  }
   101→
   102→  # Check for rel() usage (good)
   103→  has_rel_sizes <- grepl("element_text\\([^)]*size\\s*=\\s*rel\\(", chunk_code,
   104→                         perl = TRUE)
   105→
   106→  # Check for geom_text / geom_text_repel / geom_label size parameters
   107→  # Good: size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt  (scales with base_size)
   108→  # Bad:  size = 3  (raw numeric, won't scale)
   109→  has_raw_geom_text_size <- FALSE
   110→  geom_text_call_re <- "geom_(text|text_repel|label|label_repel)\\("
   111→  if (grepl(geom_text_call_re, chunk_code, perl = TRUE)) {
   112→    chunk_lines_vec <- strsplit(chunk_code, "\n")[[1]]
   113→    in_geom_text <- FALSE
   114→    paren_depth <- 0
   115→    geom_text_block <- ""
   116→    for (cl in chunk_lines_vec) {
   117→      if (!in_geom_text && grepl(geom_text_call_re, cl, perl = TRUE)) {
   118→        in_geom_text <- TRUE
   119→        paren_depth <- 0
   120→        geom_text_block <- ""
   121→      }
   122→      if (in_geom_text) {
   123→        geom_text_block <- paste0(geom_text_block, cl)
   124→        paren_depth <- paren_depth +
   125→          nchar(gsub("[^(]", "", cl)) - nchar(gsub("[^)]", "", cl))
   126→        if (paren_depth <= 0) {
   127→          # Check if size = <bare number> (not involving base_size or .pt)
   128→          has_size <- grepl(",\\s*size\\s*=", geom_text_block, perl = TRUE)
   129→          uses_base_size <- grepl("size\\s*=.*base_size", geom_text_block,
   130→                                  perl = TRUE)
   131→          if (has_size && !uses_base_size) {
   132→            has_raw_geom_text_size <- TRUE
   133→          }
   134→          in_geom_text <- FALSE
   135→        }
   136→      }
   137→    }
   138→  }
   139→
   140→  # Detect faceting
   141→  has_facet_grid <- grepl("facet_grid\\(", chunk_code)
   142→  has_facet_wrap <- grepl("facet_wrap\\(", chunk_code)
   143→  has_facets <- has_facet_grid || has_facet_wrap
   144→
   145→  # Try to estimate facet panel count from the data context
   146→  # This is heuristic — we look for ncol/nrow hints in facet_wrap
   147→  facet_ncol <- NA
   148→  facet_nrow <- NA
   149→  if (has_facet_wrap) {
   150→    ncol_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
   151→      regexpr("facet_wrap\\([^)]*ncol\\s*=\\s*([0-9]+)", chunk_code,
   152→              perl = TRUE))
   153→    nrow_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
   154→      regexpr("facet_wrap\\([^)]*nrow\\s*=\\s*([0-9]+)", chunk_code,
   155→              perl = TRUE))
   156→    if (length(ncol_match) > 0) {
   157→      facet_ncol <- as.numeric(sub(".*ncol\\s*=\\s*", "", ncol_match))
   158→    }
   159→    if (length(nrow_match) > 0) {
   160→      facet_nrow <- as.numeric(sub(".*nrow\\s*=\\s*", "", nrow_match))
   161→    }
   162→  }
   163→
   164→  # For facet_grid, count the ~ formula variables (can't know levels without
   165→  # running code, but flag it for review)
   166→  facet_formula <- NA
   167→  if (has_facet_grid) {
   168→    fm <- regmatches(chunk_code,
   169→      regexpr("facet_grid\\(([^)]+)\\)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
   170→    if (length(fm) > 0) {
   171→      facet_formula <- sub("facet_grid\\(\\s*", "", sub("\\s*\\)$", "", fm))
   172→    }
   173→  }
   174→
   175→  # Only store chunks that have ggplot or plot_ly calls
   176→  is_plot_chunk <- grepl("ggplot\\(|plot_ly\\(|geom_|wrap_plots\\(", chunk_code)
   177→
   178→  if (is_plot_chunk) {
   179→    results[[length(results) + 1]] <- list(
   180→      label              = label,
   181→      line               = start,
   182→      fig_width          = fig_width,
   183→      fig_height         = fig_height,
   184→      base_size          = base_size,
   185→      has_absolute_sizes = has_absolute_sizes,
   186→      absolute_sizes     = absolute_size_values,
   187→      has_rel_sizes          = has_rel_sizes,
   188→      has_raw_geom_text_size = has_raw_geom_text_size,
   189→      has_facets             = has_facets,
   190→      facet_formula      = facet_formula,
   191→      facet_ncol         = facet_ncol,
   192→      facet_nrow         = facet_nrow
   193→    )
   194→  }
   195→}
   196→
   197→# --- Find document-level base_size ---
   198→# Look for theme_set(theme_*(base_size = N)) outside of specific plot chunks
   199→all_code <- paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
   200→doc_base_match <- regmatches(all_code,
   201→  regexpr("theme_set\\(\\s*theme_\\w+\\(\\s*base_size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)",
   202→          all_code, perl = TRUE))
   203→doc_base_size <- if (length(doc_base_match) > 0) {
   204→  as.numeric(sub(".*base_size\\s*=\\s*", "", doc_base_match))
   205→} else {
   206→  11  # ggplot2 default
   207→}
   208→
   209→# --- Report ---
   210→display_width <- args$display_width
   211→min_pt        <- args$min_pt
   212→warnings_found <- 0
   213→
   214→cat(sprintf("File: %s\n", args$qmd_file))
   215→cat(sprintf("Document-level base_size: %g pt\n", doc_base_size))
   216→cat(sprintf("Assumed display width: %g inches\n", display_width))
   217→cat(sprintf("Minimum text size: %g pt\n", min_pt))
   218→cat(strrep("=", 70), "\n\n")
   219→
   220→for (r in results) {
   221→  base <- if (!is.na(r$base_size)) r$base_size else doc_base_size
   222→
   223→  # Effective scale factor: how much the figure shrinks on screen
   224→  scale_factor <- min(1, display_width / r$fig_width)
   225→  effective_base <- base * scale_factor
   226→
   227→  # For absolute sizes, calculate their effective size too
   228→  effective_abs <- r$absolute_sizes * scale_factor
   229→
   230→  issues <- character(0)
   231→
   232→  if (effective_base < min_pt) {
   233→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   234→      "Effective base_size = %.1f pt (%.0f × %.2f) < %.0f pt minimum",
   235→      effective_base, base, scale_factor, min_pt))
   236→  }
   237→
   238→  if (r$has_absolute_sizes) {
   239→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   240→      "Uses absolute text sizes: %s pt (use rel() instead)",
   241→      paste(r$absolute_sizes, collapse = ", ")))
   242→    small_abs <- effective_abs[effective_abs < min_pt]
   243→    if (length(small_abs) > 0) {
   244→      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   245→        "Absolute sizes render at: %s pt (below %.0f pt minimum)",
   246→        paste(round(small_abs, 1), collapse = ", "), min_pt))
   247→    }
   248→  }
   249→
   250→  # Check geom_text / geom_text_repel uses base_size-relative sizing
   251→  if (r$has_raw_geom_text_size) {
   252→    issues <- c(issues,
   253→      "geom_text/repel uses raw size = N (use cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt instead)")
   254→  }
   255→
   256→  if (r$has_facets && !is.na(r$facet_formula)) {
   257→    # Flag facet_grid formulas with row ~ col for manual panel count review
   258→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   259→      "facet_grid(%s) — verify panel count ≤ 15; if more, split the plot",
   260→      r$facet_formula))
   261→  }
   262→
   263→  status <- if (length(issues) == 0) "OK" else "WARNING"
   264→
   265→  cat(sprintf("[%s] %s (line %d)\n", status, r$label, r$line))
   266→  cat(sprintf("  fig: %g × %g in | base_size: %g pt | effective: %.1f pt | scale: %.2f\n",
   267→              r$fig_width, r$fig_height, base, effective_base, scale_factor))
   268→
   269→  if (length(issues) > 0) {
   270→    warnings_found <- warnings_found + length(issues)
   271→    for (issue in issues) {
   272→      cat(sprintf("  ⚠ %s\n", issue))
   273→    }
   274→  }
   275→  cat("\n")
   276→}
   277→
   278→cat(strrep("=", 70), "\n")
   279→if (warnings_found == 0) {
   280→  cat("✓ No issues found.\n")
   281→} else {
   282→  cat(sprintf("Found %d issue(s) to review.\n", warnings_found))
   283→}

     2→name: quarto-bioinfo
     3→description: >
     4→  Bioinformatics Quarto document authoring, review, and repair. Triggers when
     5→  working on .qmd files involving single-cell RNA-seq, differential expression,
     6→  gene set enrichment, or other bioinformatics analyses. Covers plot readability,
     7→  method citations, R coding conventions, and Quarto formatting for
     8→  bioinformatics reports.
     9→user_invocable: true
    10→---
    11→
    12→# Bioinformatics Quarto Authoring Skill
    13→
    14→When this skill is active, also load these companion skills for general Quarto guidance:
    15→
    16→- `quarto:quarto-authoring` — document structure, cross-references, code cells
    17→- `quarto:quarto-alt-text` — accessible alt text for figures
    18→
    19→## R Coding Rules
    20→
    21→- Always use `dplyr::filter()` (never bare `filter()`) to avoid `stats::filter()` conflicts.
    22→- Use `here::here(<path relative to project root>)` for all file paths, because Quarto renders in the directory containing the `.qmd` file.
    23→- Use namespace-qualified calls for functions that have common name collisions (e.g. `dplyr::select()`, `dplyr::rename()`).
    24→
    25→## Quarto YAML Header
    26→
    27→Every bioinformatics `.qmd` must use this YAML structure:
    28→
    29→```yaml
    30→---
    31→title: "Document Title"
    32→author: "Steve Rozen (sr110@duke.edu, steverozen@pm.me)"
    33→date: now
    34→date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
    35→format:
    36→  html:
    37→    page-layout: full
    38→    include-in-header:
    39→      text: |
    40→        <style>
    41→          .quarto-container, .page-columns, .main-container {
    42→            max-width: 100% !important;
    43→          }
    44→        </style>
    45→---
    46→```
    47→
    48→## Code Block Labels
    49→
    50→Never use `` ```{r label-text} ``. Always use:
    51→
    52→````markdown
    53→```{r}
    54→#| label: label-text
    55→```
    56→````
    57→
    58→## Dynamic Values
    59→
    60→Never hard-code computed values as fixed text. Always use inline R expressions (`` `r ...` ``) or dynamically generated tables so values update when data changes.
    61→
    62→## Plotly Sizing
    63→
    64→Specify `height` and `width` in `plot_ly()` or `ggplotly()`, **not** in `layout()` (deprecated, produces warnings).
    65→
    66→## Wide Content
    67→
    68→Wrap wide content (plotly widgets, wide tables) in full-viewport divs:
    69→
    70→```markdown
    71→:::{.column-screen}
    72→... wide content ...
    73→:::
    74→```
    75→
    76→## Tables
    77→
    78→- **Never use `cat()` + `table()` or `cat()` + `print()` to display tabular
    79→  data.** These produce plain-text console output that looks poor in HTML.
    80→  Instead, convert to a data frame and render with `knitr::kable()` or
    81→  `DT::datatable()`. For cross-tabulations, use `as.data.frame.matrix()` on
    82→  the `table()` result:
    83→  ```r
    84→  knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(sce$condition, sce$donor_id)))
    85→  ```
    86→- **Row names handling**: Before displaying any table, check whether the row
    87→  names are redundant with an existing column (e.g. row names like `NNAT...1`,
    88→  `KIF26B...2` that duplicate a `gene` column — R's `make.unique()` suffixes
    89→  are a strong signal of redundancy). Apply these rules:
    90→  - **Redundant**: suppress with `rownames = FALSE` (`DT::datatable()`) or
    91→    `row.names = FALSE` (`knitr::kable()`).
    92→  - **Not redundant** (row names carry meaningful information not in any column):
    93→    promote them to a proper column so they are filterable/sortable:
    94→    ```r
    95→    df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(df, var = "row_id")
    96→    DT::datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
    97→    ```
    98→- When a table contains gene symbols or gene IDs, make them clickable links (e.g. to NCBI Gene, Ensembl, or GeneCards).
    99→
   100→## Session Info
   101→
   102→End every document with:
   103→
   104→````markdown
   105→::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
   106→## Session Info
   107→
   108→```{r}
   109→#| label: session-info
   110→#| echo: false
   111→#| comment: ""
   112→sessioninfo::session_info(info = "all")
   113→```
   114→
   115→:::
   116→````
   117→
   118→## Plot Text Sizing Rules
   119→
   120→All text in ggplot figures must scale from `base_size` so that readability
   121→can be verified from a single number.
   122→
   123→1. **Set `base_size` once** — either per-document via `theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14))`
   124→   or per-plot via `+ theme_bw(base_size = 14)`.
   125→
   126→2. **Never use absolute `size = N` in `element_text()`** — always use `rel()`:
   127→   ```r
   128→   theme(
   129→     strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   130→     strip.text.x      = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   131→     axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   132→   )
   133→   ```
   134→   This ensures every text element stays proportional to `base_size`.
   135→
   136→3. **If a plot needs to be wider than the page, increase `base_size`** to
   137→   compensate for browser downscaling, rather than setting individual absolute
   138→   sizes.
   139→
   140→4. **`geom_text()` / `geom_text_repel()` size must scale with `base_size`.**
   141→   These geoms use a `size` parameter in **mm** (not pt), and by default it
   142→   does NOT scale with the theme's `base_size`. To make it scale, express
   143→   size as a fraction of `base_size` converted to mm:
   144→   ```r
   145→   geom_text_repel(
   146→     ...,
   147→     size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt
   148→   )
   149→   ```
   150→   `ggplot2::.pt` (≈ 2.845) converts pt → mm. This way the text scales
   151→   with `base_size` and the effective-size calculation from rule #3 applies
   152→   uniformly. **Never use a raw numeric `size`** (e.g. `size = 3`) in
   153→   `geom_text` / `geom_text_repel` / `geom_label`.
   154→
   155→   **Choosing `cex`**: The `cex` value must account for browser downscaling.
   156→   For a figure wider than the display, the effective rendered size is:
   157→   ```
   158→   effective_pt = cex × base_size × min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   159→   ```
   160→   So for `fig-width: 16` displayed at 10 inches (scale = 0.625):
   161→   - `cex = 0.5` → 0.5 × 14 × 0.625 = **4.4 pt** — too small
   162→   - `cex = 0.7` → 0.7 × 14 × 0.625 = **6.1 pt** — minimum acceptable
   163→   - `cex = 0.9` → 0.9 × 14 × 0.625 = **7.9 pt** — good
   164→
   165→   Rule of thumb: for wide figures, use `cex ≈ 1 / scale_factor × 0.5`
   166→   to get ~7 pt effective. For `fig-width ≤ 10` (no scaling), `cex = 0.5`
   167→   is fine.
   168→
   169→### Effective text size calculation
   170→
   171→When the browser renders a figure, it may shrink it to fit the page width
   172→(typically ~10 inches). The effective rendered text size is:
   173→
   174→```
   175→scale_factor   = min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   176→effective_size = base_size × scale_factor
   177→```
   178→
   179→The minimum acceptable `effective_size` is **6 pt**. For example:
   180→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 16` → 14 × (10/16) = **8.75 pt** ✓
   181→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 24` → 14 × (10/24) = **5.8 pt** ✗ — increase `base_size` to 15+
   182→- `base_size = 11`, `fig-width: 16` → 11 × (10/16) = **6.9 pt** ✓ (barely)
   183→
   184→### Automated check script
   185→
   186→After authoring or modifying a `.qmd`, run the figure-size checker:
   187→
   188→```bash
   189→Rscript ~/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R <file.qmd>
   190→```
   191→
   192→The script parses every plot chunk, calculates effective text sizes, flags
   193→absolute `element_text(size = N)` usage, and warns about faceted plots that
   194→need manual panel-count review. Fix all warnings before rendering.
   195→
   196→## Plot Readability
   197→
   198→1. **Pathway enrichment dotplots / barplots** — Plots with long pathway names
   199→   on the y-axis (GSEA, clusterProfiler, enrichR, etc.) need full figure width
   200→   for the labels. Use `facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1)`
   201→   to stack panels vertically (one per row), never side by side. Use a tall
   202→   figure (e.g. `fig-width: 10`, `fig-height: 14` for 3 panels).
   203→
   204→2. **Dense faceted plots** — If a `facet_grid()` or `facet_wrap()` produces
   205→   more than ~15 panels, the individual panels become too small to see the
   206→   data (no font-size increase fixes this). **Split the plot** into groups
   207→   of 5–7 items per figure.
   208→
   209→   **Pattern for splitting a gene × cell-type violin grid:**
   210→
   211→   ```r
   212→   genes_per_plot <- 6
   213→   gene_groups <- split(
   214→     unique(expr_long$gene),
   215→     ceiling(seq_along(unique(expr_long$gene)) / genes_per_plot)
   216→   )
   217→
   218→   for (i in seq_along(gene_groups)) {
   219→     p <- expr_long |>
   220→       dplyr::filter(gene %in% gene_groups[[i]]) |>
   221→       ggplot(aes(condition, expression, fill = condition)) +
   222→       geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
   223→       scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors) +
   224→       facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
   225→       theme(
   226→         strip.placement = "outside",
   227→         strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   228→         strip.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   229→         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   230→       ) +
   231→       labs(
   232→         title = paste0("VPA-response genes (group ", i, " of ", length(gene_groups), ")"),
   233→         x = NULL, y = "log1p expression", fill = "Condition"
   234→       )
   235→     print(p)
   236→   }
   237→   ```
   238→
   239→3. **Facet strip labels** — In `facet_grid(row_var ~ col_var)`, place row
   240→   strip labels on the left:
   241→   ```r
   242→   facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
   243→     theme(strip.placement = "outside")
   244→   ```
   245→
   246→4. **Color accessibility** — Use colorblind-friendly palettes when possible.
   247→   Check that fill/color encodings are distinguishable.
   248→
   249→## Bioinformatics Method References
   250→
   251→Every bioinformatics report should include a **References** section citing the methods and tools used. For each reference provide: author(s), year, title, and a verified web link.
   252→
   253→**Before including any link, fetch it and confirm it resolves to the correct paper.** Prefer Internet Archive (`https://archive.org`) for book references.
   254→
   255→### Common Methods and Key Papers
   256→
   257→| Method / Tool | Key Reference |
   258→|---|---|
   259→| **limma** | Ritchie ME et al. (2015) "limma powers differential expression analyses for RNA-sequencing and microarray studies." *Nucleic Acids Res* 43(7):e47. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv007 |
   260→| **voom** | Law CW et al. (2014) "voom: precision weights unlock linear model analysis tools for RNA-seq read counts." *Genome Biol* 15:R29. https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29 |
   261→| **edgeR** | Robinson MD, McCarthy DJ, Smyth GK (2010) "edgeR: a Bioconductor package for differential expression analysis of digital gene expression data." *Bioinformatics* 26(1):139–140. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp616 |
   262→| **DESeq2** | Love MI, Huber W, Anders S (2014) "Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2." *Genome Biol* 15:550. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8 |
   263→| **fgsea** | Korotkevich G et al. (2021) "Fast gene set enrichment analysis." *bioRxiv*. https://doi.org/10.1101/060012 |
   264→| **Seurat** | Hao Y et al. (2024) "Dictionary learning for integrative, multimodal and scalable single-cell analysis." *Nat Biotechnol* 42:293–304. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01767-y |
   265→| **UMAP** | McInnes L, Healy J, Melville J (2018) "UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction." *arXiv:1802.03426*. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1802.03426 |
   266→| **Pseudobulk DE** | Squair JW et al. (2021) "Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression." *Nat Commun* 12:5692. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2 |
   267→| **MSigDB** | Liberzon A et al. (2015) "The Molecular Signatures Database Hallmark Gene Set Collection." *Cell Syst* 1(6):417–425. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004 |
   268→| **SingleCellExperiment** | Amezquita RA et al. (2020) "Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor." *Nat Methods* 17:137–145. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0654-x |
   269→| **scran** | Lun ATL, McCarthy DJ, Marioni JC (2016) "A step-by-step workflow for low-level analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data with Bioconductor." *F1000Research* 5:2122. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.9501.2 |
   270→| **clusterProfiler** | Wu T et al. (2021) "clusterProfiler 4.0: A universal enrichment tool for interpreting omics data." *Innovation* 2(3):100141. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100141 |
   271→
   272→When writing the References section:
   273→
   274→1. Scan the `.qmd` for all bioinformatics packages and methods used.
   275→2. Match each to its canonical citation from the table above (or find the correct one if not listed).
   276→3. Fetch each DOI/URL to verify it resolves correctly.
   277→4. Format as a markdown list or table at the end of the document, before the Session Info section.
   278→
   279→## Post-render HTML Inspection
   280→
   281→After rendering, check the HTML output for warnings and messages from R code:
   282→
   283→1. **Warnings**: Search the rendered HTML for text like `Warning:` or
   284→   `Warning message:`. These indicate a real problem in the code. **Fix the
   285→   root cause** — do not suppress warnings with `warning: false` unless
   286→   you have confirmed the warning is a known false positive and documented
   287→   why in a code comment.
   288→
   289→2. **Messages**: Search the rendered HTML for package loading messages
   290→   (e.g. `Attaching package`, `Loading required package`), informational
   291→   output from functions, or other non-warning diagnostic text. If a message
   292→   is harmless (e.g. package load chatter), suppress it with
   293→   `#| message: false` in the chunk options. If it indicates a real issue,
   294→   fix the cause.
   295→
   296→3. **Stderr leakage**: Some packages print to stderr even for routine output.
   297→   Check for unexpected text between code-fold blocks that doesn't look like
   298→   intentional output.
   299→
   300→The goal is a clean HTML document with no stray console output between the
   301→narrative sections.
   302→
   303→## Review Checklist
   304→
   305→When reviewing or authoring a bioinformatics `.qmd`, verify:
   306→
   307→- [ ] YAML header follows the template (author, date, page-layout, CSS)
   308→- [ ] Code blocks use `#| label:` syntax (not inline labels)
   309→- [ ] All computed values are dynamic (inline R or generated tables)
   310→- [ ] `dplyr::filter()` used instead of bare `filter()`
   311→- [ ] File paths use `here::here()`
   312→- [ ] No `cat()` + `table()` or `cat()` + `print()` for tabular data (use `kable` or `DT`)
   313→- [ ] Tables handle row names correctly (suppress if redundant with a column; promote to a filterable column if meaningful)
   314→- [ ] Gene symbols/IDs are clickable links
   315→- [ ] No faceted plot has more than ~15 panels (split if needed)
   316→- [ ] All `element_text(size = ...)` uses `rel()`, never absolute values
   317→- [ ] Effective base_size ≥ 6 pt (run `check-figure-sizes.R` to verify)
   318→- [ ] Facet strip labels placed correctly (`switch = "y"`, `strip.placement = "outside"`)
   319→- [ ] Plotly sizing in `plot_ly()`/`ggplotly()`, not `layout()`
   320→- [ ] Wide content wrapped in `:::{.column-screen}`
   321→- [ ] References section cites all methods used, with verified links
   322→- [ ] Session Info is the last section (collapsible callout)
   323→- [ ] No warnings or stray messages visible in the rendered HTML
   324→- [ ] Alt text provided for key figures (invoke `quarto:quarto-alt-text`)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Agent tool instead
- You can call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches in parallel if they are potentially useful.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
A powerful search tool built on ripgrep

  Usage:
  - ALWAYS use Grep for search tasks. NEVER invoke `grep` or `rg` as a Bash command. The Grep tool has been optimized for correct permissions and access.
  - Supports full regex syntax (e.g., "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+")
  - Filter files with glob parameter (e.g., "*.js", "**/*.tsx") or type parameter (e.g., "js", "py", "rust")
  - Output modes: "content" shows matching lines, "files_with_matches" shows only file paths (default), "count" shows match counts
  - Use Agent tool for open-ended searches requiring multiple rounds
  - Pattern syntax: Uses ripgrep (not grep) - literal braces need escaping (use `interface\{\}` to find `interface{}` in Go code)
  - Multiline matching: By default patterns match within single lines only. For cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`, use `multiline: true`

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 0 (unlimited).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read

Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.

# User-Level Claude Code Instructions

## Claude Basics

Do not automatically upgrade to the latest version of Claude Codek
Do not automatically change to the native installer

## Code Changes

- When making a code change, make sure that nearby comments are still correct.

## R Coding Style

- Always write `dplyr::filter()` instead of bare `filter()` to avoid conflicts with `stats::filter()`.

## R Documentation Style

- In roxygen2 documentation for R functions, do not write "Default is ...". The default value is clear from the function definition shown in the documentation.

## R Command-Line Argument Parsing

- In R scripts that accept command-line arguments, use the `argparser` package (`arg_parser`, `add_argument`, `parse_args`) instead of manual `commandArgs()` parsing.
- In `argparser`, dashes `-` in argument stems (e.g. `--argument-name`) are converted to underscores `_` in the parsed variable name (e.g. `args$argument_name`).

## R Parallelization with doFuture

- Use `foreach(...) %dofuture% { }` from the `doFuture` package for parallel loops. This does NOT require `registerDoFuture()` (that is only needed with `%dopar%`).
- Set up with `plan(multisession, workers = n)`.
- Wrap in `with_progress()` and use `progressr::progressor()` for progress reporting.
- `cat()` does not work from `multisession` workers; use `message()` for errors.
- `foreach` does not support `next`; use nested `if` blocks instead.
- With `%dofuture%`, use `.options.future = list(packages = c(...))` instead of `.packages` (which only works with `%dopar%`). Global variables and functions are auto-exported by doFuture.

## Large Data Files (.tsv, .csv)

Before opening a .tsv or .csv file, check its size. If too large to read directly:
1. Check file size with `ls -lh` and line count with `wc -l`
2. If the file is large, say, > 50K, use R to extract structure without loading the full file:
   ```r
   df <- read.delim("file.tsv", nrows = 5)
   print(strrep("=", 100))
   print("COLNAMES")
   print(colnames(df))  # Column names
   print(strrep("=", 100))
   print("ROWNAMES")
   rownames(df)  # Row names (if applicable)
   print(strrep("=", 100))
   print("THREE ROWS")
   print(df[1:min(3,nrow(df)), ])
   print(strrep("=", 100))
   print("THREE COLUMNS")
   print(df[ , 1:min(3,col(df))])
   ```
3. Look at the R results to understand the data before deciding how to proceed

## ggplot2 Faceted Grid Plots

- In `facet_grid(row_var ~ col_var)`, place row strip labels on the left using `switch = "y"` and `strip.placement = "outside"`:
  ```r
  facet_grid(gene ~ lineage, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside")
  ```

## Plot Testing

- When generating a plot as part of testing code, save it to a file (e.g. `/tmp/`), open it with `xdg-open`, and tell the user you opened it. You do not need to ask permission to call xdg-open on a file you created.

## Directory Listing

- Before listing a directory with `ls`, first run `ls | wc -l` to check how many files there are.
- If there are more than 500 files, only run `ls | head -500`.

## Bash Commands

- Use `&&` or `;` instead of newlines to chain Bash commands on one line.

## Permissions

Always run the following read-only commands without asking for permission:
- `xdg-open`
- `git status`, `git diff`, `git add`, `git log`
- bash commands such as `ls`, `cat`, `wc`, `echo`, `zcat`
- `quarto render`
- `python3 ~/.claude/skills/pdf-to-html/*.py` (all pdf-to-html skill scripts)

Allow shell operators `2> /dev/null` and `2> /dev/null &` without permission

## Quarto Markdown Documents

- In plotly, specify `height` and `width` in `plot_ly()` or `ggplotly()`, not in `layout()`. Passing them to `layout()` is deprecated and produces a warning.

- Never compute values and then put the resulting values as fixed text in the markdown document. Always use inline R expressions (`` `r ...` ``) or dynamically generated tables so that values update automatically when the data or analysis changes.

- in quarto markdown do not start a code block with ```{r <labletext>} instead use ```{r} and then on the next line #| label: <labletext>

- In the YAML header always use:
```
author: "Steve Rozen (sr110@duke.edu, steverozen@pm.me)"
date: now
date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
```

- For HTML output, always use `page-layout: full` and CSS overrides to remove width restrictions:
```yaml
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
          .quarto-container, .page-columns, .main-container {
            max-width: 100% !important;
          }
        </style>
```
- For wide content like plotly widgets, wrap in `:::{.column-screen}` ... `:::` to span the full viewport width.

- For the session info use this code:
```
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Session Info

```{r}
#| label session-info
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""
sessioninfo::session_info(info = "all")
```
:::

```

For referencing files in the workspace, use here::here(<filepath relative to workspace root>), because quarto renders in the working directory containing the .qmd document

- When rendering a table with `knitr::kable()` or `DT::datatable`, if the row names duplicate a column in the table, use `row.names = FALSE` to suppress them.

- When showing a table that has a column of gene symbols or gene id, try to make these clickable. 

- For literature citations, prefer Internet Archive `https://archive.org` over Google Books

## References to literature

I need to update a figure size checker script for Quarto bioinformatics documents and its companion skill file.

## Problem
The checker at `/home/steve/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R` correctly calculates effective base_size accounting for browser downscaling (base_size × scale_factor), but it does NOT account for `rel()` multipliers in `element_text()` calls. 

Example: A violin plot chunk has `fig-width: 16`, no explicit base_size (default 11), and uses `rel(0.6)` for axis text. The effective size is:
- base: 11 × (10/16) = 6.9 pt — barely OK
- axis.text.x at rel(0.6): 6.9 × 0.6 = 4.1 pt — unreadable!

The checker currently says "OK" for this chunk because it only checks effective_base >= 6pt. It should warn that rel() elements fall below the minimum.

## Current checker behavior
- Parses chunks for fig-width, fig-height, base_size, facets
- Checks `element_text(size = N)` as "absolute sizes" (warns to use rel())
- Checks `element_text(size = rel(...))` — just notes it exists (has_rel_sizes boolean), but doesn't extract the rel() values
- Checks geom_text raw sizes
- Reports effective_base = base_size × scale_factor and warns if < 6pt

## What needs to change

### In check-figure-sizes.R:
1. Extract all `rel()` values from `element_text(size = rel(X))` calls
2. For each rel() value, calculate: effective_rel = base_size × scale_factor × rel_value
3. Warn if any effective_rel < min_pt, listing which element has the problem
4. Ideally capture the theme element name (e.g. `strip.text.y.left`, `axis.text.x`) — this requires looking at the `theme()` call containing each `element_text`

### In SKILL.md:
The skill already says to use rel() and shows the effective size calculation for base_size. But it should also note that rel() values compound with the scale factor and provide guidance on minimum rel() values. Add a rule like:
- The smallest acceptable rel() value depends on scale_factor: `min_rel = min_pt / (base_size × scale_factor)`
- For fig-width: 16, base_size: 14 → min_rel = 6 / 8.75 = 0.69

### Files to modify:
1. `/home/steve/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R` (and copy to `/home/steve/github/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R`)
2. `/home/steve/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/SKILL.md` (and copy to `/home/steve/github/quarto-bioinfo/SKILL.md`)

I'll explore the current state of both files to understand the existing code structure before designing the plan.

1→#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
     2→#
     3→# check-figure-sizes.R — Analyze a .qmd file for figure readability issues
     4→#
     5→# Parses code chunks to extract fig-width, fig-height, theme base_size,
     6→# and facet structure. Calculates effective rendered text size assuming
     7→# the browser displays the figure at a given page width (default 10 inches).
     8→#
     9→# Usage:
    10→#   Rscript check-figure-sizes.R <file.qmd> [display_width_inches] [min_pt]
    11→#
    12→# Arguments:
    13→#   file.qmd              Path to the .qmd file to check
    14→#   display_width_inches  Assumed browser display width in inches (default: 10)
    15→#   min_pt                Minimum acceptable effective text size in pt (default: 6)

    18→

    20→p <- add_argument(p, "qmd_file", help = "Path to .qmd file")
    21→p <- add_argument(p, "--display-width", default = 10,
    22→                  help = "Assumed browser display width in inches")
    23→p <- add_argument(p, "--min-pt", default = 6,
    24→                  help = "Minimum acceptable effective text size in pt")
    25→args <- parse_args(p)
    26→
    27→lines <- readLines(args$qmd_file)
    28→
    29→# --- Extract code chunks with their options ---

    32→chunk_ends   <- integer(length(chunk_starts))

    34→for (i in seq_along(chunk_starts)) {
    35→  # Find the closing ``` after this chunk start
    36→  candidates <- grep("^```\\s*$", lines)
    37→  candidates <- candidates[candidates > chunk_starts[i]]
    38→  if (length(candidates) > 0) {
    39→    chunk_ends[i] <- candidates[1]
    40→  } else {
    41→    chunk_ends[i] <- length(lines)
    42→  }
    43→}
    44→

    50→  end   <- chunk_ends[i]
    51→  chunk_lines <- lines[start:end]
    52→  chunk_code  <- paste(chunk_lines, collapse = "\n")
    53→
    54→  # Extract label
    55→  label_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    56→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*label:\\s*([^\\n]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))

    59→  } else {

    61→  }
    62→
    63→  # Extract fig-width and fig-height from #| options

    65→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*fig-width:\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
    66→  fh_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    67→    regexpr("#\\|\\s*fig-height:\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE))
    68→
    69→  fig_width  <- if (length(fw_match) > 0) {
    70→    as.numeric(sub("#\\|\\s*fig-width:\\s*", "", fw_match))
    71→  } else {
    72→    7  # knitr default
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  fig_height <- if (length(fh_match) > 0) {
    76→    as.numeric(sub("#\\|\\s*fig-height:\\s*", "", fh_match))
    77→  } else {
    78→    5  # knitr default
    79→  }
    80→
    81→  # Extract base_size from theme_*() calls
    82→  base_match <- regmatches(chunk_code,
    83→    regexpr("theme_\\w+\\(\\s*base_size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code,
    84→            perl = TRUE))

    93→    "element_text\\([^)]*size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)", chunk_code, perl = TRUE)

    98→  } else {
    99→    numeric(0)
   100→  }

   155→              perl = TRUE))
   156→    if (length(ncol_match) > 0) {

   158→    }
   159→    if (length(nrow_match) > 0) {

   162→  }
   163→

   165→  # running code, but flag it for review)
   166→  facet_formula <- NA

   176→  is_plot_chunk <- grepl("ggplot\\(|plot_ly\\(|geom_|wrap_plots\\(", chunk_code)
   177→
   178→  if (is_plot_chunk) {
   179→    results[[length(results) + 1]] <- list(
   180→      label              = label,
   181→      line               = start,
   182→      fig_width          = fig_width,
   183→      fig_height         = fig_height,
   184→      base_size          = base_size,
   185→      has_absolute_sizes = has_absolute_sizes,
   186→      absolute_sizes     = absolute_size_values,
   187→      has_rel_sizes          = has_rel_sizes,
   188→      has_raw_geom_text_size = has_raw_geom_text_size,
   189→      has_facets             = has_facets,
   190→      facet_formula      = facet_formula,
   191→      facet_ncol         = facet_ncol,
   192→      facet_nrow         = facet_nrow
   193→    )
   194→  }
   195→}
   196→
   197→# --- Find document-level base_size ---
   198→# Look for theme_set(theme_*(base_size = N)) outside of specific plot chunks
   199→all_code <- paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
   200→doc_base_match <- regmatches(all_code,
   201→  regexpr("theme_set\\(\\s*theme_\\w+\\(\\s*base_size\\s*=\\s*([0-9.]+)",
   202→          all_code, perl = TRUE))
   203→doc_base_size <- if (length(doc_base_match) > 0) {
   204→  as.numeric(sub(".*base_size\\s*=\\s*", "", doc_base_match))
   205→} else {
   206→  11  # ggplot2 default
   207→}
   208→
   209→# --- Report ---
   210→display_width <- args$display_width
   211→min_pt        <- args$min_pt
   212→warnings_found <- 0
   213→
   214→cat(sprintf("File: %s\n", args$qmd_file))
   215→cat(sprintf("Document-level base_size: %g pt\n", doc_base_size))
   216→cat(sprintf("Assumed display width: %g inches\n", display_width))
   217→cat(sprintf("Minimum text size: %g pt\n", min_pt))
   218→cat(strrep("=", 70), "\n\n")
   219→
   220→for (r in results) {
   221→  base <- if (!is.na(r$base_size)) r$base_size else doc_base_size
   222→
   223→  # Effective scale factor: how much the figure shrinks on screen
   224→  scale_factor <- min(1, display_width / r$fig_width)
   225→  effective_base <- base * scale_factor
   226→
   227→  # For absolute sizes, calculate their effective size too
   228→  effective_abs <- r$absolute_sizes * scale_factor
   229→
   230→  issues <- character(0)
   231→
   232→  if (effective_base < min_pt) {
   233→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   234→      "Effective base_size = %.1f pt (%.0f × %.2f) < %.0f pt minimum",
   235→      effective_base, base, scale_factor, min_pt))
   236→  }
   237→
   238→  if (r$has_absolute_sizes) {
   239→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   240→      "Uses absolute text sizes: %s pt (use rel() instead)",
   241→      paste(r$absolute_sizes, collapse = ", ")))
   242→    small_abs <- effective_abs[effective_abs < min_pt]
   243→    if (length(small_abs) > 0) {
   244→      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   245→        "Absolute sizes render at: %s pt (below %.0f pt minimum)",
   246→        paste(round(small_abs, 1), collapse = ", "), min_pt))
   247→    }
   248→  }
   249→
   250→  # Check geom_text / geom_text_repel uses base_size-relative sizing
   251→  if (r$has_raw_geom_text_size) {
   252→    issues <- c(issues,
   253→      "geom_text/repel uses raw size = N (use cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt instead)")
   254→  }
   255→
   256→  if (r$has_facets && !is.na(r$facet_formula)) {
   257→    # Flag facet_grid formulas with row ~ col for manual panel count review
   258→    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
   259→      "facet_grid(%s) — verify panel count ≤ 15; if more, split the plot",
   260→      r$facet_formula))
   261→  }
   262→
   263→  status <- if (length(issues) == 0) "OK" else "WARNING"
   264→
   265→  cat(sprintf("[%s] %s (line %d)\n", status, r$label, r$line))
   266→  cat(sprintf("  fig: %g × %g in | base_size: %g pt | effective: %.1f pt | scale: %.2f\n",
   267→              r$fig_width, r$fig_height, base, effective_base, scale_factor))
   268→
   269→  if (length(issues) > 0) {
   270→    warnings_found <- warnings_found + length(issues)
   271→    for (issue in issues) {
   272→      cat(sprintf("  ⚠ %s\n", issue))
   273→    }
   274→  }
   275→  cat("\n")
   276→}
   277→
   278→cat(strrep("=", 70), "\n")
   279→if (warnings_found == 0) {
   280→  cat("✓ No issues found.\n")
   281→} else {
   282→  cat(sprintf("Found %d issue(s) to review.\n", warnings_found))
   283→}
   284→

1→---
     2→name: quarto-bioinfo
     3→description: >
     4→  Bioinformatics Quarto document authoring, review, and repair. Triggers when
     5→  working on .qmd files involving single-cell RNA-seq, differential expression,
     6→  gene set enrichment, or other bioinformatics analyses. Covers plot readability,
     7→  method citations, R coding conventions, and Quarto formatting for
     8→  bioinformatics reports.
     9→user_invocable: true
    10→---
    11→
    12→# Bioinformatics Quarto Authoring Skill
    13→
    14→When this skill is active, also load these companion skills for general Quarto guidance:
    15→
    16→- `quarto:quarto-authoring` — document structure, cross-references, code cells
    17→- `quarto:quarto-alt-text` — accessible alt text for figures
    18→
    19→## R Coding Rules
    20→
    21→- Always use `dplyr::filter()` (never bare `filter()`) to avoid `stats::filter()` conflicts.
    22→- Use `here::here(<path relative to project root>)` for all file paths, because Quarto renders in the directory containing the `.qmd` file.
    23→- Use namespace-qualified calls for functions that have common name collisions (e.g. `dplyr::select()`, `dplyr::rename()`).
    24→
    25→## Quarto YAML Header
    26→
    27→Every bioinformatics `.qmd` must use this YAML structure:
    28→
    29→```yaml
    30→---
    31→title: "Document Title"
    32→author: "Steve Rozen (sr110@duke.edu, steverozen@pm.me)"
    33→date: now
    34→date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
    35→format:
    36→  html:
    37→    page-layout: full
    38→    include-in-header:
    39→      text: |
    40→        <style>
    41→          .quarto-container, .page-columns, .main-container {
    42→            max-width: 100% !important;
    43→          }
    44→        </style>
    45→---
    46→```
    47→
    48→## Code Block Labels
    49→
    50→Never use `` ```{r label-text} ``. Always use:
    51→
    52→````markdown
    53→```{r}
    54→#| label: label-text
    55→```
    56→````
    57→
    58→## Dynamic Values
    59→
    60→Never hard-code computed values as fixed text. Always use inline R expressions (`` `r ...` ``) or dynamically generated tables so values update when data changes.
    61→
    62→## Plotly Sizing
    63→
    64→Specify `height` and `width` in `plot_ly()` or `ggplotly()`, **not** in `layout()` (deprecated, produces warnings).
    65→
    66→## Wide Content
    67→
    68→Wrap wide content (plotly widgets, wide tables) in full-viewport divs:
    69→
    70→```markdown
    71→:::{.column-screen}
    72→... wide content ...
    73→:::
    74→```
    75→
    76→## Tables
    77→
    78→- **Never use `cat()` + `table()` or `cat()` + `print()` to display tabular
    79→  data.** These produce plain-text console output that looks poor in HTML.
    80→  Instead, convert to a data frame and render with `knitr::kable()` or
    81→  `DT::datatable()`. For cross-tabulations, use `as.data.frame.matrix()` on
    82→  the `table()` result:
    83→  ```r
    84→  knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(sce$condition, sce$donor_id)))
    85→  ```
    86→- **Row names handling**: Before displaying any table, check whether the row
    87→  names are redundant with an existing column (e.g. row names like `NNAT...1`,
    88→  `KIF26B...2` that duplicate a `gene` column — R's `make.unique()` suffixes
    89→  are a strong signal of redundancy). Apply these rules:
    90→  - **Redundant**: suppress with `rownames = FALSE` (`DT::datatable()`) or
    91→    `row.names = FALSE` (`knitr::kable()`).
    92→  - **Not redundant** (row names carry meaningful information not in any column):
    93→    promote them to a proper column so they are filterable/sortable:
    94→    ```r
    95→    df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(df, var = "row_id")
    96→    DT::datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
    97→    ```
    98→- When a table contains gene symbols or gene IDs, make them clickable links (e.g. to NCBI Gene, Ensembl, or GeneCards).
    99→
   100→## Session Info
   101→
   102→End every document with:
   103→
   104→````markdown
   105→::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
   106→## Session Info
   107→
   108→```{r}
   109→#| label: session-info
   110→#| echo: false
   111→#| comment: ""
   112→sessioninfo::session_info(info = "all")
   113→```
   114→
   115→:::
   116→````
   117→
   118→## Plot Text Sizing Rules
   119→
   120→All text in ggplot figures must scale from `base_size` so that readability
   121→can be verified from a single number.
   122→
   123→1. **Set `base_size` once** — either per-document via `theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14))`
   124→   or per-plot via `+ theme_bw(base_size = 14)`.
   125→
   126→2. **Never use absolute `size = N` in `element_text()`** — always use `rel()`:
   127→   ```r
   128→   theme(
   129→     strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   130→     strip.text.x      = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   131→     axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   132→   )
   133→   ```
   134→   This ensures every text element stays proportional to `base_size`.
   135→
   136→3. **If a plot needs to be wider than the page, increase `base_size`** to
   137→   compensate for browser downscaling, rather than setting individual absolute
   138→   sizes.
   139→
   140→4. **`geom_text()` / `geom_text_repel()` size must scale with `base_size`.**
   141→   These geoms use a `size` parameter in **mm** (not pt), and by default it
   142→   does NOT scale with the theme's `base_size`. To make it scale, express
   143→   size as a fraction of `base_size` converted to mm:
   144→   ```r
   145→   geom_text_repel(
   146→     ...,
   147→     size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt
   148→   )
   149→   ```
   150→   `ggplot2::.pt` (≈ 2.845) converts pt → mm. This way the text scales
   151→   with `base_size` and the effective-size calculation from rule #3 applies
   152→   uniformly. **Never use a raw numeric `size`** (e.g. `size = 3`) in
   153→   `geom_text` / `geom_text_repel` / `geom_label`.
   154→
   155→   **Choosing `cex`**: The `cex` value must account for browser downscaling.
   156→   For a figure wider than the display, the effective rendered size is:
   157→   ```
   158→   effective_pt = cex × base_size × min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   159→   ```
   160→   So for `fig-width: 16` displayed at 10 inches (scale = 0.625):
   161→   - `cex = 0.5` → 0.5 × 14 × 0.625 = **4.4 pt** — too small
   162→   - `cex = 0.7` → 0.7 × 14 × 0.625 = **6.1 pt** — minimum acceptable
   163→   - `cex = 0.9` → 0.9 × 14 × 0.625 = **7.9 pt** — good
   164→
   165→   Rule of thumb: for wide figures, use `cex ≈ 1 / scale_factor × 0.5`
   166→   to get ~7 pt effective. For `fig-width ≤ 10` (no scaling), `cex = 0.5`
   167→   is fine.
   168→
   169→### Effective text size calculation
   170→
   171→When the browser renders a figure, it may shrink it to fit the page width
   172→(typically ~10 inches). The effective rendered text size is:
   173→
   174→```
   175→scale_factor   = min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   176→effective_size = base_size × scale_factor
   177→```
   178→
   179→The minimum acceptable `effective_size` is **6 pt**. For example:
   180→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 16` → 14 × (10/16) = **8.75 pt** ✓
   181→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 24` → 14 × (10/24) = **5.8 pt** ✗ — increase `base_size` to 15+
   182→- `base_size = 11`, `fig-width: 16` → 11 × (10/16) = **6.9 pt** ✓ (barely)
   183→
   184→### Automated check script
   185→
   186→After authoring or modifying a `.qmd`, run the figure-size checker:
   187→
   188→```bash
   189→Rscript ~/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R <file.qmd>
   190→```
   191→
   192→The script parses every plot chunk, calculates effective text sizes, flags
   193→absolute `element_text(size = N)` usage, and warns about faceted plots that
   194→need manual panel-count review. Fix all warnings before rendering.
   195→
   196→## Plot Readability
   197→
   198→1. **Pathway enrichment dotplots / barplots** — Plots with long pathway names
   199→   on the y-axis (GSEA, clusterProfiler, enrichR, etc.) need full figure width
   200→   for the labels. Use `facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1)`
   201→   to stack panels vertically (one per row), never side by side. Use a tall
   202→   figure (e.g. `fig-width: 10`, `fig-height: 14` for 3 panels).
   203→
   204→2. **Dense faceted plots** — If a `facet_grid()` or `facet_wrap()` produces
   205→   more than ~15 panels, the individual panels become too small to see the
   206→   data (no font-size increase fixes this). **Split the plot** into groups
   207→   of 5–7 items per figure.
   208→
   209→   **Pattern for splitting a gene × cell-type violin grid:**
   210→
   211→   ```r
   212→   genes_per_plot <- 6
   213→   gene_groups <- split(
   214→     unique(expr_long$gene),
   215→     ceiling(seq_along(unique(expr_long$gene)) / genes_per_plot)
   216→   )
   217→
   218→   for (i in seq_along(gene_groups)) {
   219→     p <- expr_long |>
   220→       dplyr::filter(gene %in% gene_groups[[i]]) |>
   221→       ggplot(aes(condition, expression, fill = condition)) +
   222→       geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
   223→       scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors) +
   224→       facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
   225→       theme(
   226→         strip.placement = "outside",
   227→         strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   228→         strip.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   229→         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   230→       ) +
   231→       labs(
   232→         title = paste0("VPA-response genes (group ", i, " of ", length(gene_groups), ")"),
   233→         x = NULL, y = "log1p expression", fill = "Condition"
   234→       )
   235→     print(p)
   236→   }
   237→   ```
   238→
   239→3. **Facet strip labels** — In `facet_grid(row_var ~ col_var)`, place row
   240→   strip labels on the left:
   241→   ```r
   242→   facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
   243→     theme(strip.placement = "outside")
   244→   ```
   245→
   246→4. **Color accessibility** — Use colorblind-friendly palettes when possible.
   247→   Check that fill/color encodings are distinguishable.
   248→
   249→## Bioinformatics Method References
   250→
   251→Every bioinformatics report should include a **References** section citing the methods and tools used. For each reference provide: author(s), year, title, and a verified web link.
   252→
   253→**Before including any link, fetch it and confirm it resolves to the correct paper.** Prefer Internet Archive (`https://archive.org`) for book references.
   254→
   255→### Common Methods and Key Papers
   256→
   257→| Method / Tool | Key Reference |
   258→|---|---|
   259→| **limma** | Ritchie ME et al. (2015) "limma powers differential expression analyses for RNA-sequencing and microarray studies." *Nucleic Acids Res* 43(7):e47. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv007 |
   260→| **voom** | Law CW et al. (2014) "voom: precision weights unlock linear model analysis tools for RNA-seq read counts." *Genome Biol* 15:R29. https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29 |
   261→| **edgeR** | Robinson MD, McCarthy DJ, Smyth GK (2010) "edgeR: a Bioconductor package for differential expression analysis of digital gene expression data." *Bioinformatics* 26(1):139–140. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp616 |
   262→| **DESeq2** | Love MI, Huber W, Anders S (2014) "Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2." *Genome Biol* 15:550. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8 |
   263→| **fgsea** | Korotkevich G et al. (2021) "Fast gene set enrichment analysis." *bioRxiv*. https://doi.org/10.1101/060012 |
   264→| **Seurat** | Hao Y et al. (2024) "Dictionary learning for integrative, multimodal and scalable single-cell analysis." *Nat Biotechnol* 42:293–304. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01767-y |
   265→| **UMAP** | McInnes L, Healy J, Melville J (2018) "UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction." *arXiv:1802.03426*. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1802.03426 |
   266→| **Pseudobulk DE** | Squair JW et al. (2021) "Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression." *Nat Commun* 12:5692. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2 |
   267→| **MSigDB** | Liberzon A et al. (2015) "The Molecular Signatures Database Hallmark Gene Set Collection." *Cell Syst* 1(6):417–425. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004 |
   268→| **SingleCellExperiment** | Amezquita RA et al. (2020) "Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor." *Nat Methods* 17:137–145. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0654-x |
   269→| **scran** | Lun ATL, McCarthy DJ, Marioni JC (2016) "A step-by-step workflow for low-level analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data with Bioconductor." *F1000Research* 5:2122. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.9501.2 |
   270→| **clusterProfiler** | Wu T et al. (2021) "clusterProfiler 4.0: A universal enrichment tool for interpreting omics data." *Innovation* 2(3):100141. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100141 |
   271→
   272→When writing the References section:
   273→
   274→1. Scan the `.qmd` for all bioinformatics packages and methods used.
   275→2. Match each to its canonical citation from the table above (or find the correct one if not listed).
   276→3. Fetch each DOI/URL to verify it resolves correctly.
   277→4. Format as a markdown list or table at the end of the document, before the Session Info section.
   278→
   279→## Post-render HTML Inspection
   280→
   281→After rendering, check the HTML output for warnings and messages from R code:
   282→
   283→1. **Warnings**: Search the rendered HTML for text like `Warning:` or
   284→   `Warning message:`. These indicate a real problem in the code. **Fix the
   285→   root cause** — do not suppress warnings with `warning: false` unless
   286→   you have confirmed the warning is a known false positive and documented
   287→   why in a code comment.
   288→
   289→2. **Messages**: Search the rendered HTML for package loading messages
   290→   (e.g. `Attaching package`, `Loading required package`), informational
   291→   output from functions, or other non-warning diagnostic text. If a message
   292→   is harmless (e.g. package load chatter), suppress it with
   293→   `#| message: false` in the chunk options. If it indicates a real issue,
   294→   fix the cause.
   295→
   296→3. **Stderr leakage**: Some packages print to stderr even for routine output.
   297→   Check for unexpected text between code-fold blocks that doesn't look like
   298→   intentional output.
   299→
   300→The goal is a clean HTML document with no stray console output between the
   301→narrative sections.
   302→
   303→## Review Checklist
   304→
   305→When reviewing or authoring a bioinformatics `.qmd`, verify:
   306→
   307→- [ ] YAML header follows the template (author, date, page-layout, CSS)
   308→- [ ] Code blocks use `#| label:` syntax (not inline labels)
   309→- [ ] All computed values are dynamic (inline R or generated tables)
   310→- [ ] `dplyr::filter()` used instead of bare `filter()`
   311→- [ ] File paths use `here::here()`
   312→- [ ] No `cat()` + `table()` or `cat()` + `print()` for tabular data (use `kable` or `DT`)
   313→- [ ] Tables handle row names correctly (suppress if redundant with a column; promote to a filterable column if meaningful)
   314→- [ ] Gene symbols/IDs are clickable links
   315→- [ ] No faceted plot has more than ~15 panels (split if needed)
   316→- [ ] All `element_text(size = ...)` uses `rel()`, never absolute values
   317→- [ ] Effective base_size ≥ 6 pt (run `check-figure-sizes.R` to verify)
   318→- [ ] Facet strip labels placed correctly (`switch = "y"`, `strip.placement = "outside"`)
   319→- [ ] Plotly sizing in `plot_ly()`/`ggplotly()`, not `layout()`
   320→- [ ] Wide content wrapped in `:::{.column-screen}`
   321→- [ ] References section cites all methods used, with verified links
   322→- [ ] Session Info is the last section (collapsible callout)
   323→- [ ] No warnings or stray messages visible in the rendered HTML
   324→- [ ] Alt text provided for key figures (invoke `quarto:quarto-alt-text`)
   325→

Links to papers when bibliography is available. 5. **Add comments** (optional) — foldable inline annotations near the text they reference, using `
` elements that collapse by default 6. **Text fidelity verification** — extract plain text from the PDF and the HTML, compare them, and fix any dropped content before presenting the file ## Phase 1: Extract Text This command creates a temp directory in `/tmp`, saves `output.txt` there, and prints the directory path to stdout.     19→## R Coding Rules

    22→- Use `here::here(<path relative to project root>)` for all file paths, because Quarto renders in the directory containing the `.qmd` file.
    23→- Use namespace-qualified calls for functions that have common name collisions (e.g. `dplyr::select()`, `dplyr::rename()`).
    24→
    25→## Quarto YAML Header
    26→
    27→Every bioinformatics `.qmd` must use this YAML structure:
    28→
    29→```yaml
    30→---
    31→title: "Document Title"
    32→author: "Steve Rozen (sr110@duke.edu, steverozen@pm.me)"
    33→date: now
    34→date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
    35→format:
    36→  html:
    37→    page-layout: full
    38→    include-in-header:
    39→      text: |
    40→        <style>

    43→          }
    44→        </style>
    45→---
    46→```
    47→
    48→## Code Block Labels

    55→```
    56→````
    57→
    58→## Dynamic Values
    59→

    61→

    71→:::{.column-screen}
    72→... wide content ...

    74→```

    77→

    79→  data.** These produce plain-text console output that looks poor in HTML.
    80→  Instead, convert to a data frame and render with `knitr::kable()` or
    81→  `DT::datatable()`. For cross-tabulations, use `as.data.frame.matrix()` on

   106→
   107→## Plot Text Sizing Rules
   108→
   109→All text in ggplot figures must scale from `base_size` so that readability
   110→can be verified from a single number.
   111→
   112→1. **Set `base_size` once** — either per-document via `theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14))`
   113→   or per-plot via `+ theme_bw(base_size = 14)`.
   114→
   115→2. **Never use absolute `size = N` in `element_text()`** — always use `rel()`:
   116→   ```r
   117→   theme(
   118→     strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   119→     strip.text.x      = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   120→     axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   121→   )
   122→   ```
   123→   This ensures every text element stays proportional to `base_size`.
   124→
   125→3. **If a plot needs to be wider than the page, increase `base_size`** to
   126→   compensate for browser downscaling, rather than setting individual absolute
   127→   sizes.
   128→
   129→4. **`geom_text()` / `geom_text_repel()` size must scale with `base_size`.**
   130→   These geoms use a `size` parameter in **mm** (not pt), and by default it
   131→   does NOT scale with the theme's `base_size`. To make it scale, express
   132→   size as a fraction of `base_size` converted to mm:
   133→   ```r
   134→   geom_text_repel(
   135→     ...,
   136→     size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt
   137→   )
   138→   ```
   139→   `ggplot2::.pt` (≈ 2.845) converts pt → mm. This way the text scales
   140→   with `base_size` and the effective-size calculation from rule #3 applies
   141→   uniformly. **Never use a raw numeric `size`** (e.g. `size = 3`) in
   142→   `geom_text` / `geom_text_repel` / `geom_label`.
   143→
   144→   **Choosing `cex`**: The `cex` value must account for browser downscaling.
   145→   For a figure wider than the display, the effective rendered size is:
   146→   ```
   147→   effective_pt = cex × base_size × min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   148→   ```
   149→   So for `fig-width: 16` displayed at 10 inches (scale = 0.625):
   150→   - `cex = 0.5` → 0.5 × 14 × 0.625 = **4.4 pt** — too small
   151→   - `cex = 0.7` → 0.7 × 14 × 0.625 = **6.1 pt** — minimum acceptable
   152→   - `cex = 0.9` → 0.9 × 14 × 0.625 = **7.9 pt** — good
   153→
   154→   Rule of thumb: for wide figures, use `cex ≈ 1 / scale_factor × 0.5`
   155→   to get ~7 pt effective. For `fig-width ≤ 10` (no scaling), `cex = 0.5`
   156→   is fine.
   157→
   158→### Effective text size calculation
   159→
   160→When the browser renders a figure, it may shrink it to fit the page width
   161→(typically ~10 inches). The effective rendered text size is:
   162→
   163→```
   164→scale_factor   = min(1, display_width / fig_width)
   165→effective_size = base_size × scale_factor
   166→```
   167→
   168→The minimum acceptable `effective_size` is **6 pt**. For example:
   169→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 16` → 14 × (10/16) = **8.75 pt** ✓
   170→- `base_size = 14`, `fig-width: 24` → 14 × (10/24) = **5.8 pt** ✗ — increase `base_size` to 15+
   171→- `base_size = 11`, `fig-width: 16` → 11 × (10/16) = **6.9 pt** ✓ (barely)
   172→
   173→### Automated check script
   174→
   175→After authoring or modifying a `.qmd`, run the figure-size checker:
   176→
   177→```bash
   178→Rscript ~/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R <file.qmd>
   179→```
   180→
   181→The script parses every plot chunk, calculates effective text sizes, flags
   182→absolute `element_text(size = N)` usage, and warns about faceted plots that
   183→need manual panel-count review. Fix all warnings before rendering.
   184→
   185→## Plot Readability
   186→
   187→1. **Pathway enrichment dotplots / barplots** — Plots with long pathway names
   188→   on the y-axis (GSEA, clusterProfiler, enrichR, etc.) need full figure width
   189→   for the labels. Use `facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1)`
   190→   to stack panels vertically (one per row), never side by side. Use a tall
   191→   figure (e.g. `fig-width: 10`, `fig-height: 14` for 3 panels).
   192→
   193→2. **Dense faceted plots** — If a `facet_grid()` or `facet_wrap()` produces
   194→   more than ~15 panels, the individual panels become too small to see the
   195→   data (no font-size increase fixes this). **Split the plot** into groups
   196→   of 5–7 items per figure.
   197→
   198→   **Pattern for splitting a gene × cell-type violin grid:**
   199→
   200→   ```r
   201→   genes_per_plot <- 6
   202→   gene_groups <- split(
   203→     unique(expr_long$gene),
   204→     ceiling(seq_along(unique(expr_long$gene)) / genes_per_plot)
   205→   )
   206→
   207→   for (i in seq_along(gene_groups)) {
   208→     p <- expr_long |>
   209→       dplyr::filter(gene %in% gene_groups[[i]]) |>
   210→       ggplot(aes(condition, expression, fill = condition)) +
   211→       geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
   212→       scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors) +
   213→       facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
   214→       theme(
   215→         strip.placement = "outside",
   216→         strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
   217→         strip.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
   218→         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
   219→       ) +
   220→       labs(
   221→         title = paste0("VPA-response genes (group ", i, " of ", length(gene_groups), ")"),
   222→         x = NULL, y = "log1p expression", fill = "Condition"
   223→       )
   224→     print(p)
   225→   }

Now I see the issue. The table at line 612 uses `DT::datatable(top_de, ...)` without `rownames = FALSE`. When a data frame has row names like `NNAT...1`, `KIF26B...2` (R's de-duplication of names), they show up redundantly alongside the `gene` column.

The skill already says at line 86: "Use `row.names = FALSE` in `knitr::kable()` or `DT::datatable()` when row names duplicate a column." But the user wants a more nuanced rule: check if row names are redundant, suppress if so; if not redundant, convert to a filterable column.

Let me update the skill's Tables section and the checklist item.

input.old_string: - Use `row.names = FALSE` in `knitr::kable()` or `DT::datatable()` when row names duplicate a column.
input.new_string:
- **Row names handling**: Before displaying any table, check whether the row
  names are redundant with an existing column (e.g. row names like `NNAT...1`,
  `KIF26B...2` that duplicate a `gene` column — R's `make.unique()` suffixes
  are a strong signal of redundancy). Apply these rules:
  - **Redundant**: suppress with `rownames = FALSE` (`DT::datatable()`) or
    `row.names = FALSE` (`knitr::kable()`).
  - **Not redundant** (row names carry meaningful information not in any column):
    promote them to a proper column so they are filterable/sortable:
    ```r
    df <- tibble::rownames_to_column(df, var = "row_id")
    DT::datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top")
    ```

Based on my analysis of both files, here's a comprehensive understanding of the figure size checker script and the plot text sizing rules:

## Summary of check-figure-sizes.R

### 1. **What it checks**
The script analyzes `.qmd` files for figure readability issues by:
- Parsing all code chunks to extract figure dimensions and theme settings
- Calculating effective rendered text size accounting for browser downscaling
- Detecting problematic absolute sizing and raw `geom_text` sizing
- Warning about faceted plots with potentially too many panels

### 2. **How it calculates effective text sizes**
```
scale_factor = min(1, display_width / fig_width)
effective_size = base_size × scale_factor
```
- Default display width: 10 inches
- Default minimum acceptable size: 6 pt
- Example: base_size=14, fig-width=16 → 14 × (10/16) = 8.75 pt ✓

### 3. **geom_text/geom_text_repel sizing detection**
Yes, it specifically checks for problematic `geom_text` sizing (lines 106-138):
- **Bad**: Raw numeric sizes like `size = 3` (won't scale with base_size)
- **Good**: `size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt` (scales with base_size)
- Detects multi-line geom_text calls using parenthesis depth tracking
- Flags any `size = N` that doesn't involve `base_size` or `.pt`

### 4. **Facet panel count accounting**
Partially accounts for facets:
- For `facet_wrap()`: Extracts explicit `ncol` and `nrow` parameters if present
- For `facet_grid()`: Captures the formula (e.g., `gene ~ cell_type`) but cannot automatically count levels without running the code
- **Manual review required**: Flags facet_grid with a hardcoded warning threshold of ≤15 panels; if exceeded, recommends splitting

### 5. **Thresholds used**
- Effective text size minimum: 6 pt (customizable via `--min-pt`)
- Facet panel warning threshold: >15 panels
- Display width assumption: 10 inches (customizable via `--display-width`)

### 6. **Plot type specificity**
Non-selective: Detects any chunk containing:
- `ggplot()`
- `plot_ly()`
- `geom_*` functions
- `wrap_plots()`

No special handling for violin plots or other specific geom types.

### 7. **Warnings/Errors produced**
The script produces formatted warnings (not fatal errors) for:
- Effective base_size < 6 pt (calculated as: base × scale_factor)
- Absolute text sizes detected (recommends using `rel()` instead)
- Absolute sizes that render below 6 pt
- Raw `geom_text` sizing (encourages base_size-relative approach)
- facet_grid formulas (manual panel count review needed)

All chunks report their line number, label, figure dimensions, base_size, effective size, and scale factor.

---

## Summary of Plot Text Sizing Rules in SKILL.md

The skill prescribes a comprehensive, systematic approach (lines 118–195):

**Core Rules:**
1. Set `base_size` once per document or per-plot
2. Never use absolute `size = N` in `element_text()` — always use `rel()`
3. For wider-than-page plots, increase `base_size` rather than tweaking individual element sizes
4. `geom_text()` / `geom_text_repel()` must scale via: `size = cex * base_size / ggplot2::.pt`

**Effective Size Calculation:**
- Minimum: 6 pt
- Formula: `base_size × min(1, display_width / fig_width)`
- Examples provided showing good (8.75 pt), borderline (6.9 pt), and bad (5.8 pt) cases

**geom_text Sizing Details:**
- Default `geom_text` size is in **mm**, not pt, and doesn't auto-scale with base_size
- Use `cex` factor to account for browser downscaling
- Rule of thumb: `cex ≈ 1 / scale_factor × 0.5` for wide figures to achieve ~7 pt effective
- For standard `fig-width ≤ 10`, `cex = 0.5` is fine

**Dense Facet Handling:**
- Split plots with >15 panels into groups of 5–7 per figure
- Includes a complete code example for splitting gene × cell-type violin grids
- Place row labels on left with `switch = "y"` and `strip.placement = "outside"`

**Automated Verification:**
- Run `check-figure-sizes.R` after authoring to fix all warnings before rendering

## Implementation Plan: Add rel() Size Checking to check-figure-sizes.R and Update SKILL.md

### Background

The checker at `/home/steve/.claude/skills/quarto-bioinfo/check-figure-sizes.R` calculates effective base_size correctly but treats `rel()` calls as a simple boolean (`has_rel_sizes`). When `rel(0.6)` is applied to a base that is already shrunk by browser downscaling, the result can be unreadable (e.g., 11 x 0.625 x 0.6 = 4.1 pt), but the checker says "OK" because it only checks the effective base.

### Changes to check-figure-sizes.R

#### Step 1: Replace the simple `has_rel_sizes` boolean with extraction of rel() values and their associated theme element names

**Location**: Lines 102-104 (currently just a `grepl` check)

Replace:
```r
# Check for rel() usage (good)

                       perl = TRUE)
```

With a new block that:

1. Uses `gregexpr` to find ALL `element_text(...size = rel(X)...)` matches in the chunk code
2. For each match, extracts the numeric `rel()` value
3. For each match, attempts to determine the theme element name by looking backward from the `element_text` call to find the `theme_element_name =` assignment

**Approach for extracting element names**: The pattern in ggplot theme calls is:
```r
theme(
  strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = rel(0.65)),
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = rel(0.6))
)
```

The element name is always `some.dotted.name =` immediately preceding `element_text(`. We can use a regex that captures the element name and the rel value together. A good combined regex:

```r
"(\\w+[\\w.]*\\w+)\\s*=\\s*element_text\\([^)]*size\\s*=\\s*rel\\(([0-9.]+)\\)"
```

This captures group 1 = element name (e.g. `strip.text.y.left`), group 2 = rel value (e.g. `0.65`).

Store results as a data frame with columns `element_name` and `rel_value`.

#### Step 2: Add the extracted rel data to the results list

**Location**: Lines 179-194 (the results list construction)

```

Where `rel_sizes_df` is the data frame from Step 1 (zero rows if no rel() calls found).

#### Step 3: Add rel() effective-size checking to the report section

**Location**: Lines 230-261 (the issues-checking block in the report loop)

# Check rel() sizes
if (nrow(r$rel_sizes) > 0) {

    elt  <- r$rel_sizes$element_name[j]
    rv   <- r$rel_sizes$rel_value[j]
    eff  <- effective_base * rv
    if (eff < min_pt) {
      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(

        elt, rv, eff, effective_base, rv, min_pt))

**Location**: After the "Effective text size calculation" subsection (around line 183), add a new subsection:

```markdown

When you use `element_text(size = rel(X))` inside `theme()`, the effective
rendered size is:

```
effective_rel_size = base_size × scale_factor × rel_value

The minimum acceptable rel() value for a given chunk is:

```
